## Phase 162 (executed 2026-07-29 — the skill audit: the missing fourth audit quadrant, and what its first sweep found)

**Why this phase.** Code has `/codebase-review`, security has `/security-audit`, tests have `/test-audit`. The skills themselves had nothing — the prose that *instructs* a consuming agent had never been audited as an executable artifact, only as documentation. The gap became visible at GDP's cutover to Opus 5: a wave of defects surfaced at once, and a 2026-07-28 Fable session adjudicated them as **real defects, poorly written from the start**, not the new model misreading. The mechanism is the part worth keeping — *author and reviewer shared a model, so they shared a tolerance profile*, and prose gaps the author's charitable reading bridged were bridged identically at review time. That class is invisible to same-model review **by construction, not by oversight**.

**Home: maintainer-side, per the filed plan, and Wade re-confirmed it mid-session.** `tools/SKILL_AUDIT.md` + `tools/skill_audit_refs.py`, both mirror-excluded (`tools/*`, pinned at `tests/test_mirror_leak_gate.py`). Not `.claude/skills/`, not shipped. The graduation criteria are written into the doc and are deliberately strict, because `/test-audit` is the in-repo counterexample: Phase 80 shipped it with a *provisional* rubric and "calibrate out of provisional" has been an open checklist item ever since — shipping first did not accelerate calibration, it converted a design question into a permanent open leg carried in consumer-facing text.

**The mechanical pre-pass, and the two checks that were built, measured, and rejected.** `skill_audit_refs.py` carries three checks that are decidable without judgment: `retired-referent`, `shared-partial-missing`, `path-line-beyond-eof`. On its first run it reproduced the **site list** of two separately-filed checklist findings — all eleven `run_in_background` sites (§ High) and `auto-build:413`'s stale `claim_task.sh:55` (§ High, in the orchestrator design-pass entry) — with zero false positives. **Not "independently", and the round was right to strike that word:** `RETIRED_VOCABULARY` is hand-seeded, and the entry's own `reason` string cites the filing it came from, so the tool was *told* the token and re-derived only where it occurs. The second is weaker still — `auto-build:413` surfaces as a `path-line-verify` **worklist** row, which by the doc's own rule is never a finding. What the run demonstrates is that the mechanical layer holds a known class down at zero FP, not that it discovers classes. Two candidates were rejected **on measurement, and the negatives are recorded in both the doc and the script so they are not re-derived**: bare-filename existence (near-100% FP — illustrative names plus two deliberately-unbuilt future scripts the prose marks as such) and rooted-path resolution (**8 candidates, 0 true positives**, because a skill describes the *consumer's* tree, not this repo's). Line-number *correctness* is **not** mechanizable — `claim_task.sh:55` is a valid line that is simply not the right one — so those sites became a labelled **worklist that is never a pass and never a failure**, the distinction upstream #239 asks for on the check runner.

**The tool's first act was to expose two defects in *itself*, both found by checking it against its own documentation** — which is the argument for the self-inclusion rule, though not the one an earlier draft of this entry made. That draft said the tool found two defects *in its documentation*; the round showed **the doc was correct both times and the tool was wrong both times**, as the script's own code comment already conceded. The defects: `--loop-only` scanned all ten `_shared/` partials while loop mode ships six (`LOOP_EXCLUDE_SHARED` was never consulted), and the doc said the procedure "includes itself in its first corpus" while the tool never opened it. Both fixed. The partial-set half is pinned against `install.sh` (`test_loop_excluded_shared_matches_install_sh`) so it cannot re-drift; the self-inclusion half is pinned by a test against the corpus itself, which has no `install.sh` counterpart to check.

**Two further defects in the tool surfaced later in the phase, and the round was right that an earlier draft of this entry omitted both** — while re-asserting "zero false positives" a paragraph above them, which is exactly the shape that makes an omission load-bearing:

- **`RETIRED_VOCABULARY` was tool-blind.** It matched `run_in_background` as a bare substring and stamped every hit a *certain defect* — but `run_in_background` is a **live parameter of the `Bash` tool**; it is dead only for `Agent`. The zero-FP record was a contingent fact about this corpus (no shipped skill happens to document a backgrounded Bash call), not a property of the check, and `certain defect` is the verdict most likely to be acted on without reading the site. On a list designed to *grow*, that exposure grows with it. Entries are now `(token, context, reason)` and fire only inside a matching tool context, over an 8-line lookback because three of the eleven live sites name the tool several lines above the parameter.
- **`_locate()` was environment-dependent.** It resolved a bare basename by walking the whole repo, so a vendored `cli.py` inside `.venv` made ours ambiguous and the site was skipped **silently** — under-reporting that differs between two machines running the same command. Non-determinism in a checker is worse than either a miss or a false positive. Vendored trees are now excluded.

**The sweep.** Three fresh-context `general-purpose` auditors in isolated worktrees, one lens each — literal executor (zero charity), false-premise hunt, cross-document contradiction — over the loop-mode bundle (5 skills + 6 partials + the procedure doc). All three were given the SHA, told to read via `git show <sha>:<path>`, and required to open with the SHA reviewed; **all three echoed `e3ec05f` correctly, and two independently reported that their isolated worktree sat on `main` while the work was on a feature branch** — the § Medium worktree-from-default-branch item reproduced live, twice, by accident. Every load-bearing finding was re-verified against the tree before being acted on; nothing was taken on an auditor's word.

**What the sweep found and the phase fixed (the HIGH set):**

- **A false premise in the first paragraph both review skills present, found by all three lenses independently.** The Pre-flight said "Step 9 stages inside a `for … done` loop … so that invocation binds no rule whatever is seeded." Phase 153 unrolled those loops; Step 9 is eight plain `git add -A -- <path>` lines, and the same file says so 1,000 lines later, as do `WORKFLOW.md` § 8.2a and `install.sh`'s own keep-set comment. Phase 152 authored the sentence when the loop was real and Phase 153 removed the loop without touching it — **the fix stopped at the files where the finding was filed**, which is the class `SKILL_AUDIT.md` § Step 4 now exists to sweep. Rewritten to state what the rule *does* buy while keeping the live warning against re-collapsing the staging. The same sentence's "These four were undeclared until Phase 152" became "The last three" — `ee0b0dc` added exactly three bullets per skill — an off-by-one of precisely the class this phase audits for, repaired in passing and (until the round said so) undescribed.
- **`/contribute-convention` read the demotion ledger as promotion evidence.** Step 3 listed "appears in the `## Convention fire ledger`" as a *promotion-grade signal*. The ledger records **stale-verdicts** — rounds in which a rule fired **falsely** — and Step 9b retires a rule that accrues them across 2+ rounds. So the skill would take a rule the project had twice judged moot, render it as `recurred across Rounds N and M`, and file it upstream to `getsysop/sysop` under the human's consent as a convention earned from real use. **An affirmatively false provenance claim to a third party**, through the one flow whose entire purpose is showing provenance rather than asserting it.
- **`/security-audit` Step 3c built its scope file from a bash array nothing creates.** `printf '%s\n' "${STEP1_FILES[@]}"` — `STEP1_FILES` appears exactly once in the tree, at its own use site, and steps are separate shell calls so no earlier assignment could survive anyway. An unset array writes an empty file; `_load_scope` returns an empty **set**, not `None`; every finding then fails the membership test and lands in `out_of_scope`. The round reports `<K> ingested findings outside this round's scope`, **files nothing, and looks like a clean ingest** — the exact inverse of the flood the gate exists to prevent. Replaced with a `Write`-tool instruction (which also drops an unruled `printf`) plus an explicit non-empty check and the failure mode stated.
- **`/contribute-convention`'s checks.yml filter excluded 100% of its own candidates.** It skipped any check whose `id` "already exists in the installed base `.claude/checks.yml`" — but `install.sh` merges the overlay into the base by `id`, and `promotion-write-target.md` mandates a dual-write at promotion time, so a correctly-promoted local check is in the base **by construction**. The same document diagnoses the analogous trap for the markdown half in the *next* bullet and prescribes subtracting the overlay there; the YAML half never got its own treatment — and the round then showed the markdown remedy does not transfer, because that merge appends while this one replaces.
- **The permission guard's hard-stop printed two remedies that do not exist.** `/permissions add …` and `/permissions reload` are both **VERIFIED-FALSE** against the official docs (independent `claude-code-guide` probe): `/permissions` takes no subcommands, and no in-session settings reload exists. Two-thirds of the escape hatch shown to a *human* at the stop was dead text. Replaced with the interactive UI and edit-then-restart.
- Plus: the two review skills' dedup rules **diverged against the same index** (`±5 lines` vs exact `file:line`, while `WORKFLOW.md` § 2.6 asserts they are the same and the ±5 rule's own prose names exact-matching as the failure mode) — aligned; the pre-scan restatement template **rebound the letters of the format string it had just defined** one sentence earlier (`E of S selected`, where `S` is the *skipped* count) — fixed with the binding stated; and `test-assessment-rubric.md` attributed its three-suite bar to **`WORKFLOW.md` §5.1**, which defines *cross-round* survival within one project, citing `decomposition-rubric.md` as a completed precedent when that rubric cleared a **two**-queue bar and its own dogfood leg is still open — rewritten to own the bar instead of borrowing authority for it.

**The class sweep (Step 4) found the classes mostly contained — but its own round showed "contained" was too strong.** The sweep grepped the *loop* corpus, while Step 4's rule says the whole corpus, and the §5.1-conflation class had a sibling one directory over in `_shared/decomposition-rubric.md` (loop-excluded, so out of the swept set) — found by the round, not the sweep, and fixed there. The genuinely contained exception was the reverse case: `§ Compound findings` was cited by three shipped files and **no such heading existed** — the rule was a bolded paragraph inside `## Classification Rubric`. Given a real `###` heading so the citations resolve, rather than editing three call sites, since a rule cited by name from three files deserves to be addressable.

**The convention leg.** *(An earlier draft of this entry called this "the phase's only consumer-facing addition" — **false**, and the round caught it. Six shipped files change, and this is the **smallest**: +8/−1, against `contribute-convention`'s +30/−9 and `security-audit`'s +9/−5, both of which gain net-new normative instruction rather than corrections. Understating consumer blast radius is the class this repo tracks.)* `_shared/adversarial-review.md` § *Running more than one reviewer* now states that **model diversity matters as much as lens diversity and a model upgrade is itself a review event**: re-read the corpus on model cutovers rather than on a calendar, and where the harness offers more than one model, give at least one reviewer a different model from the author's — **conditional on the harness, never assumed**, since a consumer may have exactly one and the portable requirement is still fresh context. Stating it unconditionally would be the shape Phase 154's own round retired. Three guards added and **mutation-verified** (each mutation killed exactly one guard): deleting the paragraph, making the cross-model rule unconditional, and reverting the `Compound findings` heading.

**What was deliberately not absorbed, and why.** The sweep returned roughly twenty verified defects; the phase fixed the HIGH set and filed **twelve** as one § Medium bundle with coordinates, plus the `security_map.md` shell-header regression as its own entry (Phase 130's post-128 fix landed on `convention_map.md:10` and never on its twin, so the *security* map's shell rules match nothing on a current install). The alternative was a phase with no boundary. Two coverage gaps are **named rather than papered over**: `WORKFLOW_GUIDE.md` got zero lens coverage, and `tasks/schema.md` was not opened — the skill-vs-schema lens is recorded *not-applicable to the loop corpus*, not clean.

**One correction the phase owes its own record.** `SKILL_AUDIT.md`'s flagship worked example — the one line whose whole job is to demonstrate that line numbers need a human read — shipped its first draft saying the referent lived at `:291`, copied from the checklist entry reporting the staleness, which had copied it from `tools/CLAIM_TASK_ORCHESTRATOR_SPEC.md`. All three were wrong; `:291` is a PyYAML guard in the `--release` path and the real site is the `WORKTREE_DIR=` assignment at `:433`. **The filing written to fix a rotted line number had itself rotted.** Corrected in all three places — **but its own round then showed that was not enough.** The § High entry Phase 162 "corrected" carried **three more rotted coordinates in the same sentence-set**, untouched: the lock-existence guard cited at `:311` is at `:453`, its write cited at `:423` is at `:565`, and the `expires:` assertion cited at `:406-407` is at `:548-549`. Fixing one number in an entry and calling it corrected is the same failure one level up, and the record's "corrected in all three places" invited a reader to believe the entry was clean. All six are now resolved. The entry also gained a second defect the original filing missed: the same sentence's path formula drops the `WORKTREE_PREFIX` override the code honors.

**Round.** Commit `a897a6e`, three independent fresh-context `general-purpose` reviewers in isolated worktrees, each given the SHA, told to read via `git show <sha>:<path>`, and required to open with the SHA reviewed — all three echoed it correctly. Lenses: claim verification, record truth, regression/guard-strength. **Per the convention this phase ships, the claim-verification reviewer ran on a different model than the author** — and it immediately paid, catching two of the phase's own fixes shipping new falsehoods. Every surviving finding below was re-verified against the tree before being applied.

- **The claim lens found that two fixes replaced a falsehood with a different falsehood.** (1) The `permission-guard` remediation: having correctly retired `/permissions add` and `/permissions reload` as nonexistent, the phase wrote *"edits to a settings file are not picked up by the running session."* **False** — an independent docs probe confirms Claude Code watches its settings files and hot-reloads `permissions`; only `model` and `outputStyle` need a restart. The phase over-extrapolated "no reload *command* exists" (true) into "no reload exists" (false), which is the exact false-premise class it was fixing. (2) The `contribute-convention` checks.yml fix was **unsatisfiable by construction**: `install.sh` *removes* the colliding upstream entry and keeps the consumer's, so `base − overlay` contains none of the consumer's ids and the override branch can never fire — converting "excludes 100% of candidates" into "excludes 0%", which would send Sysop's own shipped rules back to Sysop as novel, with round provenance attached. Its stated rationale was false too: the markdown merge *appends* (so subtraction leaves something to compare), the YAML merge *replaces*. Rewritten to resolve against the source clone, or to **refuse to guess** and route to the human. (3) The shipped model-diversity paragraph overclaimed three times — *"this is measured"* (it is one incident, not a measurement), *"more rounds of the same model do not find it"* (**falsified by this very phase**, whose same-model lenses found Phase-152-authored text), and a bare "the corpus" with no antecedent in the shipped partial. Rewritten to state the honest mechanism: the correlation is a tendency, and what breaks it is an explicitly hostile lens — a different model is the cheaper way to get that independence, not the only one.
- **The record lens found the phase's own prose overstating in three headline places.** "The convention leg, the phase's **only** consumer-facing addition" — false; six shipped files change and it is the **smallest** of them. "The tool's first act was to find two defects **in its own documentation**" — inverted; the doc was right both times and the tool was wrong both times, as the script's own comment already conceded. "**Independently** reproduced two separately-filed findings" — the token is hand-seeded from the filing it cites, so what was re-derived is the site list, not the finding; and the second surfaced only as a *worklist* row, which by the doc's own rule is never a finding. It also caught that the record omitted the two later tool defects (the tool-blind `RETIRED_VOCABULARY` and the environment-dependent `_locate`) while re-asserting "zero false positives" a paragraph above them, four coordinate/attribution errors, and — the sharpest — that **the § High entry this phase "corrected" still carried three more rotted coordinates in the same sentence-set** (`:311`→`:453`, `:423`→`:565`, `:406-407`→`:548-549`). Fixing one number and writing "corrected in all three places" is this phase's own thesis, one level up, landing on the phase.
- **The regression lens ran 67 self-designed mutations: 52 killed, 15 survived (22%).** Five were material and are now closed, each re-verified by re-running the surviving mutation: **Check 1 had no live-tree guard at all** — the very check the flagship example is about — so a planted beyond-EOF referent made the checker exit 1 while the suite stayed green; `PATH_LINE_RE`'s extension breadth was unpinned (narrowing it to `.py` passed everything while silently dropping two of three real worklist rows, including the `claim_task.sh` referent this phase spent its record correcting); `main()`'s `--loop-only` wiring was never exercised (every test called `corpus()` directly); the beyond-EOF comparison had no boundary test, so `>` → `>=` survived and would false-flag every citation to a file's last line; and **the phase's own new predicate constant was vacuous** — emptying `_MODEL_UPGRADE_IS_A_REVIEW_EVENT` left the guard passing, the one predicate in that module without the non-vacuity twin every sibling has. Eight further survivors are latent (no delta on today's corpus) and are filed rather than guarded.
- **The same lens held the phase to its own Step 4 and found the sweep missed its own flagship class, twice.** The `for … done` "binds no rule" falsehood the phase fixed in two skills **survives in a third** — `review-close/SKILL.md:26` states it *about* the two that were fixed — and the phase's Step 4 grep never searched for it, having swept five other classes instead. The `§5.1` misattribution likewise survived in `_shared/decomposition-rubric.md` at **both** `:5` and `:103`, in the file the fix itself cites as precedent. And the phantom-shell-variable class was live in `auto-build`: `PLAN_TEXT` and `RAW_FINDINGS` are documented as *subscripted, context-held* values (`PLAN_TEXT[<TASK_ID>]`) and used as bare `"$PLAN_TEXT"`, never assigned — writing **empty** `plan.md`/`review.md` into the archive the skill calls "the *only* record of why the task parked" and "the **durable** record". Verbatim the `STEP1_FILES` shape, missed because the sweep's regex matched only the array-expansion form. All four fixed.
- **One fix of the phase's own was actively harmful and is corrected.** The new non-empty scope-file gate used `wc -l`, which counts *newlines*: a one-path file with no trailing newline returns `0`, and the instruction beside it says an empty list means "treat the round as `--full`" — dumping the whole-repo backlog into a scoped round, which is the precise flood the gate exists to prevent. Now `grep -c .`, with the reason stated.

**Gate.** Suite re-run green after the round fixes. The round's five material mutation survivors were each re-run against the new guards and each now kills exactly one.

## Phase 163 (executed 2026-07-29 — the skill-audit checker becomes a gate: a baseline that names its debt, and wiring that does not depend on remembering)

**Why this phase.** Phase 162 shipped a checker whose own docstring says *"a check enforced only by a reader remembering to look is not a check"* — and then left it in exactly that state. Its own adversarial round said so: nothing invoked it, and it **exited 1 on the real tree**, because the eleven filed `run_in_background` sites were still open § High work in the checklist and had never been accepted by the tool. (An earlier draft said they were "accepted as debt in the checklist" — **false**, and it retro-fitted this phase's decision onto the prior record. Phase 162's round explicitly filed the choice as unmade: *fix them, or baseline them*. Baselining is a decision made **here**, on Wade's call, not a fact inherited from the filing.) Those two facts compound — an unwired checker is merely unhelpful, but a red one *cannot* be wired, so the second defect was quietly protecting the first. Wade's call: baseline the eleven, wire the checker.

**The baseline is deliberately not shaped like `.claude/checks_baseline.txt`.** The house format is `check_id|path:line`, and it is the wrong key here for a reason the house already documents: `run_checks/baseline.py`'s `_is_coverage` carve-out gives line drift as its first reason — the line number "is *diff-relative* — it shifts every commit, so a baselined coverage gap would never re-match on the next PR" — though the docstring then says "**More to the point**" and ranks a different reason above it (a coverage gap must never be accepted as debt at all). Only the drift half transfers here. Skill markdown has the same property for the same reason — it is edited constantly, so a line-keyed entry rots on the first unrelated edit *above* it. Upstream #235 makes the same *observation* in passing — a baseline that is "`file:line`-keyed and rots when a line moves" — though note what it actually asks for is an **inline waiver that composes with** the baseline, not a replacement for it, and it endorses the baseline for exactly the historical-debt use this phase puts it to. The rot is real; #235 is not a filed objection to line-keyed baselines, and an earlier draft here said it was.

So the key is **`(check, file, detail, count)`**, where `detail` is the retired token, the cited path, or the missing partial — never a line number. The **count** is what keeps a line-free key honest, and it is the part worth keeping: a bare `(check, file)` key would suppress a *twelfth* `run_in_background` in an already-baselined file, which is the failure mode that makes coarse baselines worse than none. With the count, occurrence twelve is `NEW` and fails.

**Two asymmetries — and the round was right that calling them "chosen rather than inherited" overstated both.** Naming rather than counting is what `run_checks` already does (`cli.py` prints `[baseline] <msg>` per suppressed finding), and it never fails on a stale entry either. What is genuinely new here is *reporting* staleness at all, which `run_checks` does not do. The two properties still matter and are stated deliberately; they are adopted from the house, not invented against it. A defect that gets **fixed** shows up as a `STALE BASELINE` entry and **never fails the run** — ratcheting down must not break the build, which is the surface-never-reap house style the orchestrator design pass identified across four advisory thresholds. And baselined defects are **named, not merely counted**: the output lists file, check, detail and multiplicity, because a baseline that prints only a number is how accepted debt becomes invisible debt. A damaged baseline line fails **closed** — it is skipped, so its findings resurface as new, rather than being read as a blanket allow, which is the silently-green failure upstream #238 calls strictly worse than no gate.

**Wiring: pytest, not CI and not `self_check.sh`.** Both are the wrong home, but for **two different reasons**, and an earlier draft bundled them as one. `self_check.sh` genuinely ships, so it would be calling a script consumers do not have. CI does not ship — its problem is that `.github/workflows/` **is** mirrored, so a CI step would break the public snapshot unless guarded. And "cannot call it" was too strong: this phase's own `corpus()` reaches for a `tools/` file behind an existence guard, so either home *could* be guarded the same way. The honest claim is a cost/benefit one — a guarded call in either place would never fire for consumers and buys nothing over pytest, which already runs every phase. `tests/test_skill_audit_refs.py` already runs every phase and already carries the mutation-verified mirror skip, so the gate costs no new surface. **State its reach precisely, because an earlier draft of this sentence did not:** the gate fires when a `(check, file, detail)` key's count *exceeds* its allowance. It does **not** fire when slack created by fixing one baselined occurrence absorbs a newly-added one — the round falsified the draft's "fails the moment a new dangling referent enters the skills tree" with a single experiment. Within an already-baselined key the gate detects **net growth**, not replacement. That is the ordinary property of a count-keyed baseline and the price of a line-free key; it is stated here rather than discovered later. Accepting one deliberately means running `--update-baseline`, which puts the acceptance in a **reviewable diff** rather than in someone's memory.

**Two fixes to this phase's own drafts — not prior bugs, and the round was right to press on the framing.** Neither flag existed before this commit, so "originally" below means *earlier in this phase*, not in a predecessor. The second is also weaker than a bug: it is reachable only by a caller that repoints `REPO_ROOT`, which in practice means the tests. `--update-baseline` originally snapshotted whatever corpus the flags selected, so `--update-baseline --loop-only` would have dropped every lifecycle-skill entry and widened the baseline to "clean" for eleven defects it never looked at. It now always snapshots the **full** corpus regardless of `--loop-only`, with a guard. Also fixed: the `--baseline` default resolved against the import-time `REPO_ROOT` rather than the current one, so a caller pointing at another tree would silently read the wrong baseline.

**And the referent Phase 162 verified but never actually repaired.** `auto-build/SKILL.md:413` still cited `claim_task.sh:55` — Phase 162 confirmed it was wrong and corrected **three** record surfaces — the checklist entry, `tools/SKILL_AUDIT.md`, and `tools/CLAIM_TASK_ORCHESTRATOR_SPEC.md` — while leaving the referent itself live. The sharper version, which the round supplied: Phase 162 **edited that very file**, 41 lines of it, and still walked past the citation it had just verified as wrong. Now fixed by **symbol, not line** (the `WORKTREE_DIR=` assignment), per the lesson that phase drew; the stated path formula also regains the `WORKTREE_PREFIX` override it had been dropping. Three smaller things the round found undescribed and are now stated: `--no-baseline` shipped untested and undocumented (both closed); the `--json` contract changed (`defects` now means *new* defects, with `baselined` and `stale_baseline` alongside); and the output block was renamed `CERTAIN DEFECTS` → `NEW DEFECTS`, because what fails a run is a defect being unbaselined rather than being certain.

**Round.** Commit `2727982`, three independent fresh-context `general-purpose` reviewers in isolated worktrees, each given the SHA and required to echo it — all three did. Lenses: **defeat-the-baseline** (attack the suppression mechanism directly), **guard strength** (an independent mutation set), and **claim/record truth**. The first ran on a **different model than the author**, per the convention Phase 162 shipped. This was the harshest round any phase here has had, and the two headline findings are the same one seen from opposite sides.

- **The phase's flagship invariant was false at the surface the phase itself designated as the enforcement point.** "Fixing a defect must not break the build" is asserted in six places — and running the ratchet exactly as the tool's own `STALE` output instructs turned the suite **red**, because two tests hardcoded the counts (one of them added by this phase). The checker honored the asymmetry; the pytest wiring — chosen *because* it runs every phase — did not. Both tests now derive from the baseline, so the baseline is the single source of truth and `--update-baseline` is a complete workflow. **The first fix for this reintroduced the same bug in the same edit**: the new `--no-baseline` test hardcoded 11.
- **The checklist claimed leg (b) resolved and it was not.** The phase struck through *"nothing pins the script's existence"* and wrote "(a) + (b) resolved", while adding no such assertion — every test routed through the mirror skip, so deleting `tools/skill_audit_refs.py` left **36 skipped, suite green**. A false resolution claim, and worse than the original defect, because striking the item removes the prompt to fix it. Closed properly now with an assertion outside the skip guard, keyed on a mirror-excluded marker so it fires only in the source repo.
- **The guard-strength lens ran 65 mutations of its own: 25 survived (38%)** — the highest survivor rate recorded here, and the honest number. The core was sound (40 kills: the parser, `tally`, the `<=` comparison in both directions, the full-corpus guard, the exit paths for tested flags). The survivors clustered where the phase had not looked: **the committed baseline could be widened to 400/400/300 with a green suite**; the "no line numbers in the key" guard tested `baseline_key()`, a function that takes no line, while two of the three `report.defect(..., detail)` call sites — where the rot risk actually lives — were unguarded; the `NEW DEFECTS` listing body, the `BASELINED` block's detail, the `--json` contract this phase reshaped, and `write_baseline`'s overwrite-not-append behaviour were all unasserted. Nine guards added; each was verified by re-running the surviving mutation, and **one of them survived its first version** — a constant `detail` passed a check that only asked for non-empty and line-free, so the guard now requires `detail` to *discriminate* between two distinct partials in one file.
- **The defeat-the-baseline lens found the count claim was per-line, not per-occurrence.** Two occurrences on one line left the tally unchanged, so a new site added to an already-flagged line was suppressed — falsifying "a twelfth occurrence raises the count and fails" at three shipped sites. Now counted per occurrence. It also found `--loop-only` reporting all three lifecycle entries as *"fixed since baselining"* on every run (the write side got the full-corpus guard; the read side did not), a unicode-digit count that crashed rather than skipping (`"²".isdigit()` is True, `int("²")` raises), a `.tmp` left behind on a failed rename, and a misattributed line in the `NEW DEFECTS` report — the positional split named a long-baselined line as the new one, so the finding now says the occurrences are indistinguishable and lists every site.
- **Seven record claims were overstated and are corrected in place.** "Fails the suite the moment a new dangling referent enters" — false; slack from a fixed occurrence absorbs a new one, and the gate sees *net growth within a key*, never replacement. "The eleven were accepted as debt in the checklist" — false; they were open § High work, and baselining is a decision made **here**. "Two asymmetries, both chosen rather than inherited" — naming-not-counting is what `run_checks` already does. "Two correctness fixes found while wiring" — both were fixes to this phase's own drafts, neither flag existed before this commit. "Both are the wrong home for the same structural reason" — two different reasons, and "cannot call it" is refuted by this phase's own existence-guarded `tools/` read. The `_is_coverage` quotation was not verbatim and promoted the source's secondary reason to primary. And **upstream #235 was restated stronger than it is** — it asks for an inline waiver that *composes with* a baseline and endorses the baseline for exactly this use; it is not a filed objection to line-keyed baselines.
- **Two record surfaces disagreed with each other, and one filed defect this phase fixed was left standing as open.** The § High entry still read as untouched work while a gate silently suppressed it — now annotated that the sites are baselined, not fixed. And § Medium leg (d), whose first half this phase repaired, was neither ticked nor annotated.
- **One shipped sentence was wrong about its own subject.** The new `auto-build` text said the line number had been "stale for four phases" — four phases *moved* it (29 → 32 → 91 → 156 → 159b), but it was stale for ~131. Corrected: understating the persistence of the exact defect class the sentence exists to warn about is the worst place to be imprecise.

**Gate.** Suite green after the round fixes; the round's own surviving mutations were each re-run against the new guards and each now kills at least one.

## Phase 164 (executed 2026-07-29 — the lifecycle skill audit, blind: 6,152 lines, five lenses, and a calibration result that failed in the direction nobody planned for)

**Scope, set before anything was spawned: sweep + triage + cut, zero fixes.** Every verified defect became a filed entry rather than a same-phase patch. The reason is Phase 162's: a phase that audits *and* fixes hands its own round two jobs, and Phase 162's round caught two of its fixes shipping fresh falsehoods. **This is a third deviation, and the round was right that it went uncounted while every other deviation was meticulously logged:** `tools/SKILL_AUDIT.md`'s Step 4 is titled *"fix, then sweep the class"*, so a zero-fix run departs from the procedure it claims to execute. The brief's `fix → mirror push → video` sequencing is the real license, not the two-jobs argument — and the two-jobs argument cuts both ways, since Phase 162's round *caught* its bad fixes, which is evidence the two-job round works. The cost is stated rather than left implicit: **the `cleanup_worktrees.sh --force` prescription this record calls data loss stays live in shipped skills until the fix wave.** The full run record — per-lens findings, class site counts, the coverage ledger — is [`tools/LIFECYCLE_AUDIT_2026_07_29.md`](./tools/LIFECYCLE_AUDIT_2026_07_29.md). This is the second corpus, which satisfies graduation criterion #1.

**The corpus was derived, not copied.** `install.sh:88`/`:92` give 18 skills at exactly 6,152 lines plus 4 partials at 443; the brief's block matched. `guided-mode` is reachable only through prose in `claim-task` and `auto-build`, so a `_shared/`-path grep alone misses it — worth recording because that is how a partial gets left out of a sweep that believes it was complete.

**Step 1 was green and its worklist paid off negatively, which is still a result.** 0 new defects, 11 baselined. The one in-corpus `path-line-verify` item — `claim-task:564`'s citation of `parse_subagent_envelope.py:402` — was assigned to the literal lens and came back **sound**. So that check scored 1 checked, 0 defects here: directed attention that correctly directed nowhere.

**Two deviations from the brief, both deliberate, both recorded rather than silent.** First, **the auditors were not given `tools/SKILL_AUDIT.md`**, which the brief says to execute. That document names four known defects verbatim — the `run_in_background` class, #243's `/sitrep` premise quoted in full, the Phase-159a `TASK:` grammar, `claim_task.sh:55`. Handing it to a blind auditor is seeding dressed as procedure. The round corrected the framing: the first draft called this "a hole in the brief", but the brief's blind constraint already bans issue text and paraphrases from any auditor prompt, and `SKILL_AUDIT.md` contains them — so withholding it was **compliance, not discovered diligence**. At most the brief carries an ambiguity worth one sentence. What the deviation framing did obscure is a real question the record still owes: the auditors executed lens definitions stripped of the procedure's surrounding discipline (unit-of-review, the Step-5 ledger rules), and nothing here measures what that subtraction cost. The three lens blockquotes were quoted verbatim; the rest of each prompt was authored from the lens definition and the file list. Second, **model diversity went to the round rather than the sweep**, on `_shared/adversarial-review.md:26`'s own argument that a zero-charity literal instruction is what breaks the correlation — and because splitting a lens pair across model families would confound the per-lens FP rate criterion #2 wants *measured*. The blind guarantee was **mechanical for the seven untracked issues** — all five prompts launched before they were read — and **intentional (no-paste discipline) for the ten already transcribed in `REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md`** and the four defects `SKILL_AUDIT.md` names. The first draft claimed the mechanical form for all of it, which is a stronger guarantee than the mechanism provides.

**Lens 3 was not split, and the ledger says so.** Cross-document contradiction's whole capability is holding the corpus at once; a split lens 3 cannot see a `claim-task`/`review-close` disagreement, which is its highest-value class. Lenses 1–2 are therefore split evidence and lens 3 is whole evidence, and those are not interchangeable rows.

**The flagship class is the one Phase 162 swept too narrowly: 20 confirmed phantom shell-variable sites in 2 files** — `auto-build` 18 (`$WORKTREE_PATH`×9, `$TASK_ID`×4, `$PRE_PLAN_HEAD`×2, `$PRE_EXEC_HEAD`, `$BRANCH_NAME`, `$SUBSET_IDS`) and `claim-task` 2. Both the literal and false-premise lenses converged on it independently. Two consequences are severe and verified: `auto-build:444`'s `[ "$NEW_HEAD" != "$PRE_PLAN_HEAD" ]` is always true with the right side empty, so the Phase-6a integrity check **parks every task in the batch unconditionally**; and an empty `$SUBSET_IDS` makes `/auto-build TECH-A TECH-B` select from the whole frontier, inverting Step 1's stated "never silently dropped" invariant. Filtered out honestly: `review-close`'s `$APPROVED_BRANCH`×6 is *documented* (`:727` instructs re-export) and `main-push-guard`'s `$EXPECTED_BRANCH`×2 is a *declared template*. **[Corrected by Phase 169 — both exclusions were wrong, and the word "honestly" is the part that aged worst.** `:727`'s note scoped itself to Steps 4a–4d, which contain **zero** `$APPROVED_BRANCH` references; all six sites are in Step 4-pre, in two blocks *after* the one that assigns it, so the note prescribed nothing for them. They expanded empty on every run and took the whole PR-reuse shape out of service silently. `main-push-guard`'s "declared template" had no declaration anywhere in the file — only a comment defining what the value *means*, written in variable syntax where the repo's idiom is `<angle brackets>`. This record's own § *and its round* had already retracted the first one ([`tools/LIFECYCLE_AUDIT_2026_07_29.md`](./tools/LIFECYCLE_AUDIT_2026_07_29.md)) — **the retraction never propagated to this sentence or to `REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md`, which is how a corrected finding still sent the next phase the wrong count.** Both are fixed; the real class was 33 sites, not 20.]

**The sweep's own regex was wrong twice, and that is the phase's most transferable lesson.** A comment reading `# SUBSET_IDS = …` matched the assignment pattern and hid `$SUBSET_IDS` entirely — the very site a lens had just reported — and `$VAR` references inside comments were counted as phantoms, producing three false positives including `review-close:1008`, which is a comment explaining why the code deliberately does *not* read `$RUN_ID`. **A class sweep's regex is itself a claim, and it needs verifying like any other.** Phase 162's failure was not carelessness about sweeping; it was trusting an unverified regex, and that failure recurred here inside the phase built to prevent it.

**The brief's thesis was demonstrated on the friction-log path.** Ground truth is `install.sh:2877` → `sysop/SYSOP_ISSUES.md`. Three sites still assert the **repo root** outright (`review-close:1171`, `onboard:147`, `intake:177`) plus seven bare. `REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md` § Medium leg (k) already filed *one* site, a bare one; Phase 147 logged a "live Phase-128 friction-log path drift" rider. **The path has been fixed twice without a class sweep, and three wrong-root assertions survived both.** `review-close:1171` is the worst: it is the *find* step, its absence branch concludes "consumer pre-dates Phase 13", and the note it prints tells the human to re-run `install.sh` — which skips an existing file, so the false diagnosis is self-confirming.

**Eleven further HIGH findings were verified against the tree by hand**, of which three deserve naming. `cleanup_worktrees.sh --force` is prescribed at three sites as the rollback "on the orphan", but its usage is `[--clean | --force]` with **no path operand**, it skips no ACTIVE worktree, and it `git worktree remove --force`s every non-main one — so a single failed claim destroys every concurrent claim's uncommitted work, and `auto-build:802` additionally claims it "clears the lock" when the script contains no lock path. `review-close:34` justifies a deliberate allow-rule omission by asserting the Phase-36 `PermissionDenied` hook will surface the `!`-escape for a denied `mkdir`/`cp`; the hook has exactly three matchers, all `git push`/`git commit`. And `review-close:383`'s doc-only skip covers `### Always` — "build, full test suite, project-level smoke tests" — on the reasoning that "a doc-only diff can't regress code-level lint/typecheck", while **31 test modules in this repo assert on `SKILL.md` prose**.

**Two findings were downgraded rather than rejected, which is what Step 3 is for.** The literal lens's F6/F7 each bundled a checkable structural claim with an unproven consequence — that certain shell shapes defeat an allow-rule, so the block is auto-denied. That consequence asserts as settled the exact question `REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md:74` records as open. Accepting them as framed would have written that open question into this file as fact, the Phase-153 shape; rejecting them as units would have discarded a real finding, since `review-close:49` forbids "no capture into a variable" and Step 4-pre `:697` and Step 4d `:995` each contain one. A file forbidding a shape it then uses is a self-contradiction independent of matcher behaviour, so both survived re-framed.

**The calibration failed, and it failed in the direction the brief did not plan for.** Scored against the 17 known open issues: **1 re-derived blind** (#220, whose exact mechanism the literal lens found), 5 correctly out of corpus, 2 adjacent, and **9 missed in corpus**. The sharpest data point is a miss — **#243, the motivating example for lens 2's existence, quoted in `SKILL_AUDIT.md`'s own lens definition, is still live at `sitrep/SKILL.md:48`, and lens 2 had that file in corpus and examined 10 justification clauses in it.** The brief hoped the sweep would re-derive the known defects and thereby measure the lenses; instead it measured something more useful and less welcome: **the lenses find a different population than issue triage does** — roughly 35 verified findings no issue names, against 1 clean re-derivation out of 12 in-corpus knowns. So the sweep is a complement to reading the issue list, never a substitute. **Three claims first written here were retracted by the round.** (i) *Recall arithmetic.* "9 missed in corpus" scored `#249` and `#265` as misses while the same commit logs them **unverified**, and counted `#250` as missed although its headline clause is refuted against our tree. An unverified issue cannot be scored as a miss — not finding a non-defect is correct behaviour. Rescored against verified issues only the figure is roughly **6 misses of ~9–10 verified in-corpus knowns**; the conclusion (recall is poor) survives, the precision did not. (ii) *FP rate.* The claim that criterion #2's FP half is now satisfied does **not** hold: ~35 of ~132 raised findings were adjudicated, so the low rejection count is computed over an orchestrator-selected subsample — estimation by another name — and the five auditor reports were session artifacts that are not preserved anywhere in the tree, so "recorded per-report" describes evidence a later reader cannot open. **Criterion #2 is unsatisfied on both halves, not one.** (iii) *The explanation.* "Different populations" was asserted without eliminating two causes that implicate this phase's own choices. The stronger candidate, found by the round, is **lens mis-specification**: lens 2's prompt said "Check X independently against the tree", and `#243`'s premise is falsified by the *harness*, not by anything in the tree — so an auditor following the lens literally is pointed away from its own motivating example. The other is that removing model diversity from the sweep (deviation 2) is the founding theory's own predicted failure, and **this run cannot exclude it**. Also unrecorded, and it changes the fix: whether `sitrep:48` was among the 10 clauses lens 2 reported examining. If it was not, the sharpest data point is a coverage gap rather than a detection failure.

**The blocking cut, and the criterion had to be repaired before it could be applied.** The brief's candidate — *does a day-one loop-mode consumer hit this?* — has a sharp edge: **every skill in this corpus is in `LOOP_EXCLUDE_SKILLS` by definition**, so a literal reading makes the entire audit non-blocking by construction. That is not a reductio; it is very nearly the right answer, and it is why the criterion needed a second and third clause rather than replacement: **(a)** does a day-one loop-mode consumer hit it, **(b)** would it break or falsify something the announce itself demonstrates or claims, **(c)** is it unrecoverable data loss, which is blocking on any path. Under clause (a), **scoped to the 17 known issues plus this audit's findings, and with `#264` still unverified**, the only confirmed member is `#235` — the `severity: critical` grep check that silently does not fire in every consumer running the python or postgres pack, and loop mode ships both. The round forced three corrections to what was first written here. First, the original text said "no finding from this audit qualifies under (a)", which is **false**: the Class-2 sweep found sites in `report-issues` (`:294`, `:320`), and `report-issues` is loop-shipped — a tree-wide class sweep reaches outside the corpus by design, so it can and did produce clause-(a) candidates. Second, "the brief's prior guess survives its own test" was scored under clause (a) alone — the very clause this paragraph argues is inadequate. Testing a hypothesis with the test you just discredited is not survival: under the **full** repaired criterion the prior guess does not hold, because the set is `#235` plus the `cleanup_worktrees.sh --force` data loss unconditionally (clause c) plus two conditional on the demo's scope (clause b). Third, the blocking set was stated inconsistently **inside one commit** — this paragraph named three clause-(b)/(c) additions including `review-close:1171`, while the § High filing named four different ones and filed `:1171` under § Medium. **The single reconciled set is now in `REVIEW_CHECKLIST.md` § High with the qualifying clause named per item**, and that filing is authoritative over any list here. That the elastic clause (b) produced two different answers in one sitting is the strongest available evidence that a three-clause criterion does not terminate deterministically, and it is recorded as a limitation of the cut rather than smoothed over. Whether (b) binds depends on what the demo video actually shows — loop mode only, or the lifecycle as well — which is Wade's call and is recorded as the open decision rather than assumed.

**Gate.** Adversarial round run post-commit per `CLAUDE.md` — three fresh-context reviewers in isolated worktrees (claim-verification, reasoning-soundness on a different model family, completeness), each given `2447bb8` and required to echo it. **The round's first finding was against this line.** The committed text read "Adversarial round run per `CLAUDE.md`; findings and their disposition recorded below" — written *before* the round, so at the only revision it existed in it was false twice over: no round had run, and nothing was recorded below. That is the Phase-153 class (a false claim already sitting in the record) written about **the gate itself**, in the phase whose entire product is the record. It is corrected here rather than quietly, because the convention's stated reason for writing prose pre-round is that the round must be able to catch exactly this, and it did.

**What the round found, and it went badly for the phase.** Three reviewers, ~50 findings, and the phase's central failure was its own: **two HIGH findings were filed as single sites and never class-swept** — the `PermissionDenied` over-promise (6 sites, `review-close:1084` missed and worse than the filed `:34`, since it covers `gh pr`, the dominant close path under `pr` policy) and `cleanup_worktrees.sh --force` (6 sites, plus a root cause at `WORKFLOW.md:1807` whose § 8.4 row omits `--force` and is pinned by a test). **Both were reachable with a one-line grep from the inventories this phase built as its countermeasure**, so the failure was never about tooling — it was treating a filed finding as finished, which is the exact recurrence the brief exists to stop and the exact way Phase 162 failed. **The sharpest single finding was that the flagship count's boundary rested on a false premise:** six `$APPROVED_BRANCH` sites were excused by citing `review-close:727`, whose own sentence scopes itself to "Steps 4a–4d" while all six sites are in Step 4-pre and 4a–4d contains none — so a lens-2-class false premise in a shipped skill was adopted as authority rather than flagged, by the phase running the false-premise lens. **Seven further claims were retracted**, including one HIGH struck outright (`ui-verify:103`/`:108`, where a reviewer executed both calls and both succeeded — a runtime failure inferred from a schema keyword and filed as verified), two false counts (`auto-build` does state the fallback; `fixable` appears once, not zero), the recall arithmetic (2 unverified issues and 1 refuted one counted as misses), criterion #2's FP half (unsatisfied — ~35 of ~132 adjudicated and the auditor reports not preserved), and the coverage denominators (not re-derivable, no script committed). **The round also supplied a better explanation for the `#243` miss than the phase had:** lens 2's blockquote enumerates *because / since / so that*, and `sitrep:48` carries none of them — so the lens points away from its own motivating example. That is **mis-specification, not poor recall**, and it is a fixable instrument rather than a mysterious result. **The deliverable had also not reached the gate it exists for** — the cut lived only in prose and is now filed under `## Before announce` with the mirror-push debt, and the "Net:" line that still called the video the only load-bearing item is amended.

**Suite green after the round fixes: 1859 passed, 4 skipped** (the four skips are pre-existing — no pre-namespace `install.sh` commit exists on a branch). Pre-pass still exits 0 with 0 new defects. Mirror push deliberately **not** performed — 161–163 remain unpushed, deferred to after the fix wave on the brief's cost argument, and must not slip past the announce.

## Phase 165 (executed 2026-07-29 — Wave 1 item 1: the `cleanup_worktrees.sh --force` data loss, and a round that falsified the phase's own account of its fix)

**The defect, at source.** `cleanup_worktrees.sh:23` is `ACTION="${1:-list}"` — only `$1` is ever read. There is no path operand and no single-target mode; `--force` (`:191–227` pre-fix) loops every non-`MAIN` entry from `git worktree list --porcelain` and runs `git worktree remove --force` on each, with none of the ACTIVE skip `--clean` applies at `:153`. Three skill sites nonetheless prescribed it as the rollback "on the orphan" (`claim-task:337`, `auto-build:415`, `auto-build:802`), so **one failed `/claim-task` would have destroyed every concurrent claim's uncommitted work.** That is a capability, verified by execution against the pre-fix script — not a recorded incident; no incident exists in this tree, and an earlier draft of this entry wrote it in the simple past, which the round caught. `/auto-build` Step 8 additionally told the human the command "clears the lock"; `grep -in lock` on the pre-fix script returns one comment and no lock path, so the task was left `in_progress` + locked with no workspace and `claim_task.sh --entry-state` returns `held` (`:86`, `:183`) forever.

**The design fork, decided on evidence: reshape the callers, do not teach the script a scoped mode.** A correct single-target remover already exists **twice**, lock-aware in both: `claim_task.sh --release` (worktree at `:315`/`:322`, lock `rm -f` at `:390`) and `batch_work.sh --release` (`:579`/`:585`, lock at `:256`). A scoped mode here would have been a *third* remover — path-scoped but state-blind, strictly worse than the two that exist, and a second owner for a job that already has one. `git worktree remove <path>` is meanwhile the established house idiom for "this one worktree": inside both `--release` paths, printed by `sitrep_survey.py:649`, in `claim_task.sh:295`'s manual recipe, offered by `install.sh:3902`. It is already allow-listed (`core/companion/.claude/settings.json:14`), so the fix adds no permission rule. Its plain form refuses on uncommitted or untracked changes, which *is* `--clean`'s ACTIVE-skip precedent for "safe", delivered without inventing anything.

**The rollback prose had to split in two, because the lock is written last.** `claim_task.sh` mutates in the order branch (`:489`) → worktree (`:500`) → lock (`:565`), and `--release` **hard-gates on the lock existing** (`:267–273`). A single replacement command would therefore have been wrong: on a Step-4c validator failure the full claim exists and `claim_task.sh --release <TASK_ID>` is exactly right (it reports the already-`open` status left by the rollback's `git checkout` as an info line, `:356` → `:377`, rather than an error); but on a Step-4b failure *after* `git worktree add` and *before* the lock write — the case `claim-task:337` is conditioned on — `--release` refuses, and only `git worktree remove <path>` applies. Both branches are stated at the site, along with two preconditions the first draft omitted and the round supplied: `--force` must precede the task ID (`claim_task.sh:229–233` rejects a trailing flag, so the natural `--release <ID> --force` hard-fails), and the index flip needs a PyYAML-capable `python3` on `PATH` or it exits having changed nothing.

**The class, swept: 6 `--force` prose references, and the belief's licence was upstream of all six.** Three prescribed wrongly; three are descriptions, none of them a prescription (`auto-build:504`, `auto-build:789`, `WORKFLOW.md:1846`) — so `:504`'s contradiction with `:415`, filed as part of the defect, resolves by fixing `:415`: `:504` was the correct pole and is byte-identical pre and post. An earlier draft called all three "correct descriptions of the wholesale semantics", which the round falsified using this phase's own guard: two of them state no scope at all, and the marker set had a `"surviv"` entry existing only to admit them. Both now state the scope outright and `"surviv"` is gone. Upstream sits `WORKFLOW.md:1807`, the § 8.4 canonical scripts row, which read `` `cleanup_worktrees.sh [--clean]` | List or remove merged worktrees `` — `--force` absent from the table entirely and "merged" the wrong premise the three sites acted on. Calling that the *root cause* is an inference, not a traced authoring link: a row that never mentions `--force` cannot have taught anyone what `--force` does, so what it did was **fail to prevent** the belief. That is still worth fixing and guarding, on the narrower claim. Five `--clean` prescriptions were checked; two of them (`WORKFLOW.md:366`, `:572`) turned out to carry the same narrowed "merged" premise and are now corrected too, which an earlier draft had waved through as "verified correct". `docs/`, `README.md` and `packs/` have zero references.

**A filed premise corrected, empirically.** The item asserted that `tests/test_workflow_scripts_table.py` pins the misleading § 8.4 row, "so the misleading description is guarded by a test." **It does not.** That guard's `ROW_SCRIPT` regex (`:42`) captures the filename only and discards the signature and the whole description cell. Verified by restoring the pre-fix row and running the guard: **3 passed** — reproduced independently by two reviewers. The row was *unguarded*, not test-anchored, which made it cheaper to fix than filed. (Precisely: the filing's claim that the test "pins that row **set**" is true — it pins which script names appear; its *conclusion* that the description is therefore guarded is the false step.)

**One script change, and the round rescoped what it is worth.** An operand is now rejected before anything is pruned or removed, with the error naming the three single-target owners. The first draft of this entry called that "the item's failure shape" and claimed that ignoring `$2` "is what made the wrong belief expressible as a runnable command." **Both are wrong, and the round proved it by reading the pre-fix sites:** all three wrote the command **bare**, with the targeting only in prose, and the bare form destroys exactly as much — so this guard does not block the shape that shipped. What closed the defect is the prose reshape plus the § 8.4 row. The operand rejection is defence-in-depth against the natural next move of a reader who believes such prose, which is to append the path they mean; it is cheap, fails closed, and no legitimate invocation pays for it. `--force` also now names the uncommitted work it destroys — driven by a real `git status --porcelain` check, **not** by the ACTIVE class, because ACTIVE is `classify_worktree`'s fallthrough and so covers pristine unmerged and pristine detached-HEAD worktrees: the first version fired falsely on every clean unmerged worktree, including the `/auto-build` EXECUTED ones whose work is safely committed, and a reviewer measured 2 of 4 warnings false by executing `--force` over five differently-shaped worktrees. Making `--force` *skip* ACTIVE was rejected on a different ground: the classifier emits only MAIN/MERGED/ACTIVE/STALE, so `--force` minus ACTIVE is **exactly** `--clean` (which already removes STALE — an earlier draft's "`--clean`+STALE" was wrong and the argument is stronger without it), leaving no way to do what the flag advertises.

**Guards, and an honest statement of what they cannot do.** The real safety net is the script: `--force <path>` exits 1, so that belief is non-executable whatever a document says. The prose guards are defence-in-depth, and the round rebuilt them. They had matched **per physical line**, which four ordinary authoring habits walked straight through — a backslash line-continuation, naming the flag before the script, a shell variable, and a list step with the command fenced and the flag in following prose — so matching now runs over whitespace-collapsed text with a proximity window unioned with the mention's whole line. The runnable-form check had also required a literal `bash ` prefix, while `WORKFLOW.md`'s own prescriptive house style omits it; it now keys on the path separator instead. And the searched population had covered only `core/skills` and `core/companion/docs` while **`install.sh` already prescribes this script twice** — a guard excluding a file in the population it exists for — so `install.sh`, `README.md`, `docs/` and `packs/` are now searched and the population is itself pinned. Three holes remain and are named in the module rather than left to be discovered: a bare-form prescription that *admits* its own scope passes (distinguishing prescription from description is a coherence judgement, not a pattern); the § 8.4 row guard is a **reversion** guard, since a rewrite can carry all eight required substrings and assert the opposite; and a flag held in a variable far from the invocation escapes the window.

**Mutation verification: 24 real mutations, 24 killed, 0 unexpected survivors, plus 3 documented residuals that behaved as documented.** That supersedes the first draft's "9 mutations, 9 killed, 0 survivors", which the round classified as **self-selected — and it was right**: 4 of those 9 were "revert the text I just wrote" against guards written to assert exactly that text, so they could not fail; the set tested the one hole the guard docstring itself named and never probed the assumption both guards shared. The new set includes every mutation the round found surviving (the four authoring habits, the no-`bash` path form, the incidental-marker laundering, the narrowed population, the operand check moved below `git worktree prune`, the `${1}`-for-`${2}` message, an `exit 0` stub script, and the ACTIVE-keyed loudness regression). Three of my own mutation attempts were themselves buggy — the vacuity case failed to remove the token it claimed to remove, twice, because `--forcex` still contains `--force` — which is the same lesson Phase 164 recorded one level down: **a mutation is a claim and needs verifying like any other.** Worth keeping: both pre-existing tests that exercise `--force` (`TestForceNeverRemovesMain`, Phase 84; `TestForcePreservesUnmergedBranch`, added Phase 105) create exactly *one* secondary worktree, so **neither could distinguish "removes ALL non-main" from "removes the one I named"** — the misreading itself was invisible to the suite. `TestForceIsWholesale` uses two.

**Suite: 1871 passed, 4 skipped** (baseline 1859 + 12 guards — 7 in `test_cleanup_worktrees_sh.py`, 5 in the new `test_worktree_removal_scoping.py`; the four skips are pre-existing — no pre-namespace `install.sh` commit exists on a branch). The phantom-variable sweeper reports `auto-build`'s `$TASK_ID` at ×4 on the same lines before and after these edits, byte-identical output. A first draft used `"$TASK_ID"` in the Step-5 abort **prose** at `:415`; the round established that the sweeper walks fenced blocks only, so that would have added **no** site — the change to the `<TASK_ID>` placeholder form its neighbours use is consistency, not a near-miss, and an earlier draft's claim that it "would have added a 6th site" was wrong in both the arithmetic and the premise.

**Round.** Four fresh-context `general-purpose` reviewers in isolated worktrees on distinct lenses — fix correctness, guard vacuity (on a different model from the author, per `_shared/adversarial-review.md`), record truth, and an independent class re-sweep — each given `087c897` and required to echo it. **All four landed on `f9eaeda` rather than the target**, the caveat that section documents at `:37`; all four detected it, read the target through `git show 087c897:<path>` or their own scratch checkout, and said so loudly, so their findings stand. The round was expensive for the phase and worth it. What held: the inventory (an independent re-sweep re-derived the same 6/3/3 and named no missed site), every one of ~30 `file:line` citations, the suite arithmetic (1868 = 1859 + 9, reproduced in a clean clone), the archive move (byte-for-byte identical, 1612 chars), the `CLAUDE.md` row at 179 characters, the permission surface, the whole branch→worktree→lock / lock-gate / already-`open` triad the new prose rests on, and the headline correction about the unguarded row. What did not: **two defects the fix itself introduced** — the script comment's "it removes worktrees and nothing else" (false: both modes `git branch -d`, every mode prunes) and the § 8.4 row's parenthetical defining ACTIVE as "anything with uncommitted or untracked work" (false, and it taught the wrong inference the loudness bug rested on) — plus the operand-framing overreach, the ACTIVE-keyed loudness, the missing `--force` flag position, the missing PyYAML precondition, `/auto-build` Step 8 leaving `main` dirty with no instruction to commit the flip, the branch-only-orphan gap and missing branch cleanup at `claim-task`, the two `--clean` sites still carrying the "merged" premise, the `--clean`+STALE error, the Phase-84 provenance error, a `grep` cited as evidence that no longer reproduces in the commit shipping it (this phase's own guard message now contains the phrase), and eight guard bypasses. All were fixed or explicitly documented as residual before merge.

**The round also widened the class past this phase's framing, and three of those are filed rather than fixed** (§ High): `/review-close:1109`'s `git reset --hard origin/main`, which is ungated tree-wide in the main checkout while its prose explains only which commits it discards — the identical shape one site over, on the maintainer's daily path since this repo's `main` is PR-protected; a worktree holding only gitignored content, which classifies MERGED and is destroyed silently by `--clean` too; and `claim_task.sh --release`'s bare-`python3` PyYAML probe, which makes the newly-prescribed remedy inert on venv-only consumers including this machine. A fourth, `review-close:70`'s claim that `/auto-judge` and `/document-work` cleanup paths reach for `git worktree remove --force` when **no shipped skill contains that string at all**, was fixed here rather than filed (and the replacement's first draft cited `grep … core/skills/` — a source-repo path that does not exist in a consumer install, and would have been the only such reference in the shipped skills tree; the same class again, caught on a self-review pass rather than by a reviewer): it is the second member of the same wrong-capability class whose first member was `:802`'s "clears the lock", and answering the sweep's own question with "there is another one, filed for later" is how this repo has shipped the same defect three times.
